verdict.rationale: RudderStack's own Tracking Plans feature is documented to flag violations on incoming data automatically and to act on non-compliant events at the source, with marketing copy describing catching issues in transit and filtering data before it reaches downstream teams. However, the evidence is headline-level only: there is no detailed documentation of how blocking or dropping is configured, and no quarantine or dead-letter handling is shown. missing for 10: detailed docs on violation-handling modes (block/drop vs. forward-with-flag), quarantine of violating events, schema/tracking-plan definition depth, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a data engineer, a tracking plan or schema is enforced — violating events get flagged, blocked, or quarantined instead of silently corrupting downstream data

citations.quote: Tracking Plans Monitor and act on non-compliant event data at the source
Define your ideal state with shared data definitions and automatically flag violations on incoming data.
Set predefined tracking plans to catch issues in transit, then fix and filter data before it impact downstream teams.
Validate and fix new or bad data in-flight before it is loaded into your data lake or warehouse for modeling and training.
